answer: Each account must anchor its identity to a surveyed tundra plot where a shale marker is placed. A satellite image verifies the marker's coordinates and unique pattern; the registrar issues one account per marker and rejects duplicate coordinates. Extra identities require extra plots and markers at cost C per epoch, so n sybils earn n(R-C) per epoch, unprofitable when C>R. Assumption: the satellite verifier and registrar are honest; marker forgery or plot-sharing is the weakness.
